item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
260
ABPZ20 KNHC 161721
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Fri Oct 16 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane Trudy, located a
few hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression could form during the latter half of next week
while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward over the
eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 13a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 161748
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 13A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
...SATELLITE WIND DATA SHOWS TRUDY IS WEAKER THAN INDICATED 
PREVIOUSLY...
...HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT ABOUT TO INVESTIGATE THE HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.7N 102.5W
ABOUT 230 MI...370 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 320 MI...515 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...110 MPH...175 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 335 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...963 MB...28.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Playa Perula
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo southward to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo southward to Zihuatanejo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area.  A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous.  Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required later today or tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located
near latitude 14.7 North, longitude 102.5 West. Trudy is moving
toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A north- 
northwestward to northwestward motion at a slightly faster forward 
speed is forecast during the next few days. On the forecast track, 
the center of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico on Saturday and pass near the coast Saturday 
night into Sunday.
 
Recent satellite wind data shows that Trudy is not as strong 
as indicated in the previous advisory. Maximum sustained winds are 
near 110 mph (175 km/h) with higher gusts.  Some strengthening 
could occur through Saturday, and Trudy is forecast to be a major 
hurricane when it makes its closest approach to Mexico. Weakening is 
predicted later this weekend and into early next week. An Air Force 
Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft is currently approaching Trudy.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140
miles (220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 963 mb (28.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning
area by late Saturday or Saturday night, with tropical storm
conditions spreading across the area on Saturday. Tropical storm
conditions are expected within the Tropical Storm Warning area by
late tonight or early Saturday. Hurricane conditions are possible in
the Hurricane Watch area by late Saturday, with tropical storm
conditions beginning on Saturday. Tropical storm conditions are
possible in the Tropical Storm Watch area on Sunday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 15 inches along and near
the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
Mexican coast in Guerrero. This rainfall may result in localized
flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas along steep
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern Mexico and will spread northward toward west-central
Mexico during the next few days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 161456
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026

Satellite imagery shows that Trudy's intensification has again 
paused, with the eye becoming less distinct and the convective cloud 
tops in the eyewall becoming warmer. An earlier GPM microwave 
overpass suggested that the eyewall has opened up on the south side, 
possibly due to a tongue of dry air wrapping into that part of the 
hurricane.  The various satellite intensity estimates have changed 
little since the last advisory, so the initial intensity is held at 
105 kt.  An Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft is scheduled 
to investigate Trudy later today.

The initial motion is a somewhat erratic 335/4 kt, as Trudy has 
followed its previous westward jog with a northward jog. A gradual 
turn toward the northwest is likely during the next 24 hours as a 
weak low-level to mid-level ridge builds over eastern Mexico. This 
motion should continue through about 72 hours, with the center 
passing near or over the coast of west-central Mexico at about the 
48 hour point. After that time, a weakening Trudy should be steered 
more by low-level flow. However, the guidance has some spread as to 
which direction that should be. Some of the guidance shows a 
west-northwest or west motion, while some models steer the cyclone 
more northward due to the influence of a large deep-layer trough 
over the northeastern Pacific. This part of the forecast track 
splits the difference by showing a slow west-northwestward motion. 
Overall, the new forecast track is similar to the previous track 
through 60 hours, and then is a little to the north of the previous 
track.

While the environment that Trudy is in seems to be conducive for 
strengthening, the intensification has sputtered twice during the 
past day or so. And in an interesting twist, the regional hurricane 
models do not forecast any additional strengthening before the 
hurricane reaches a less favorable environment. Other intensity 
guidance suggest some intensification could still occur, and based 
on a blend of this and the previous forecast the new intensity 
forecast shows some strengthening during the next 24 hours. Trudy is 
still expected to be a major hurricane as it approaches the coast of 
Mexico. Later in the forecast period, Trudy is expected have land 
interaction, move into a drier air mass, and encounter increasing 
southwesterly shear. These factors should cause steady to rapid 
weakening, and the new forecast follows the previous forecast in 
showing the system as a post-tropical low by 120 h.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane when it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, bringing
an increasing risk of storm surge, damaging winds, and flooding
rain. Hurricane Warnings and Watches, as well as Tropical Storm 
Warnings and Watches, are currently in effect for portions of the 
coast, and additional watches and warnings will likely be required 
later today or tonight.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the 
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, 
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 37
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 161457
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  37
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Southwesterly vertical wind shear and dry mid-level air are taking a 
toll on Simon this morning. An earlier AMSR-3 microwave pass 
indicated that the mid-level center was displaced to the northeast 
of the low-level center, a trend also reflected in bursts of deep 
convection to the north and east of the center over the past 
several hours. The pass also suggested that the low-level center 
was slightly farther north than previously estimated, and the 
initial position was adjusted accordingly. The latest TAFB Dvorak 
intensity estimate was 2.0/30 kt. However, convective organization 
has changed little, so the intensity is maintained at 35 kt for this 
advisory. 

Simon is moving northwestward at 315/8 kt. Given the storm's shallow 
nature, its motion is being steered by the low- and mid-level flow, 
characterized by troughing to the west and a mid-level ridge to the 
northeast. This general motion is expected to continue over the next 
24-36 h, bringing Simon parallel to the coast of Baja California 
Sur. Following the northward adjustment of the initial position, the 
latest NHC track forecast has been shifted slightly to the right of 
the previous forecast and lies near the corrected consensus (HCCA) 
track. 

Despite moving over very warm waters (28-30 C), significant 
southwesterly wind shear and increasingly dry mid-level air are 
expected to support continued weakening. In fact, simulated 
satellite imagery from the ECMWF and GFS suggest that Simon may 
struggle to maintain organized deep convection by late tonight. The 
official forecast calls for Simon to become a post-tropical remnant 
low within 24 h, though this transition may occur sooner. 
Dissipation is expected by 48 h.
